name: Opus Momentum
strategy: Cross-sectional price momentum ranked on 12-1 and 6-month returns: long the energy E&P leader (XOP), a trimmed AI-semiconductor core (SMH plus NVDA) and newly qualifying healthcare (XLV), against the two persistent losers, long-duration Treasuries (TLT) and homebuilders (ITB).
reassessment_note: The 10-14 to 10-16 chip selloff stopped out AMAT and pushed SMH 10.5% lower on the week. A dated 10-15 report ties the selloff to inflation data that reinforced Fed rate-hike bets. I re-ranked about 35 ETFs and coins from Yahoo daily closes (12-1, 6m, 3m, and distance from the 50/200-day averages) instead of relying on the packet alone. Web search found almost no coverage dated to this week, so the rebalance rests mainly on the price data. Changes: (1) GEV is removed because its 6m (-7%) and 3m (-11%) returns no longer qualify it as a momentum long, even though its 12-1 return is still high. (2) SMH is cut from 30% to 22%: it still ranks near the top on 12-1 (+63%) and 6m (+16%), but it is 6.8% below its 50-day average and negative over 3m, which is the setup for a momentum crash in a hiking regime. (3) XOP is raised from 15% to 20% as the strongest asset on both 6m and 12-1, above both moving averages. (4) XLV is added at 10% because it now qualifies (6m +20%, 12-1 +18%, above both averages). (5) The ITB short goes from 12% to 14% because ITB is the worst equity sector on every window and is rate-sensitive. TLT short is kept. Cash rises to 16% to absorb the reduced semiconductor risk.

positions.thesis: Top-ranked asset in the universe on 6m (+24%) and 12-1 (+56%), 7% above its 50-day and 20% above its 200-day average, and it rose 4.6% in a week when SPY fell 2%. It is the purest momentum signal available, so it becomes the largest leg. The 12% stop sits outside its normal weekly range but caps an oil reversal.

Still the strongest equity complex on 12-1 (+63%) and positive on 6m (+16%), so a 12-1 momentum rule keeps it. But it fell 10.5% this week on rate-hike repricing and is now 6.8% below its 50-day average. Cut from 30% to 22%, with a tighter 12% stop measured from the new entry, so that a full momentum crash costs about 2.6% of NAV rather than 4.5%.

Held through the selloff better than the semiconductor index (-6.6% on the week against SMH -10.5%, and +3% over 3m against SMH -5%), which shows relative strength inside the complex. Kept at 8% as the highest-quality single name in the AI leadership group, now that AMAT has been stopped out.

New entrant on the momentum screen: 6m +20%, 12-1 +18%, 1m +4.7%, above both its 50-day and 200-day averages, and up in a week when tech fell. This adds a leadership group with low correlation to semis and oil and diversifies the long side away from the two crowded themes.

The weakest US equity sector on every window measured (6m -14%, 12-1 -14%, 3m -14%) and 10.6% below its 200-day average. Rising hike odds keep mortgage rates high. Raised from 12% to 14% as the cleanest momentum loser.

Negative on 12-1 (-10%), 6m (-8%) and 3m (-5%), and below its 200-day average. The inflation data driving hike bets is the macro reason this loser should keep losing. It also partly hedges a growth-scare rally against the long book. Kept at 10% with a tight 8% stop because bonds rallied 2.7% this week on risk-off flows.
